why: The statement is one universal yes/no question, so any credible non-sofic countable group answers it in full (whole, refuted, counterexample). For the OpenAI August event the close call is verification: Fournier-Facio, a named group theorist, says publicly in his arXiv acknowledgements that he went through the argument with Bradford and Dogon, and then built on it. Under F9 a named expert working through the argument in public counts, so I marked it digested. The Lean build and the Sienicki audit, which disclaims reconstruction, add nothing to that. The priority and provenance disputes are about credit, not correctness, so the event stays credible. Its AI role is generated because OpenAI credits the model with the construction. The Fournier-Facio and Kun–Thom follow-ups each exhibit non-sofic groups, so they are whole, refuted and unreviewed. Kun–Thom's ChatGPT use has no systems entry, so its AI role is none. Conditional results, surveys and closure results are scored none. The IRS paper and the random-graph paper are variants. Berlai proves soficity for a restricted family, so it is a case. The repository event (openai-math-197) is whole but doubtful, because its non-soficity claims are side corollaries resting on an unexecuted computation.
doubts: The 'digested' call on the OpenAI event rests on a single acknowledgement sentence from Fournier-Facio. Read strictly, the event would be unreviewed (claimed). OpenAI's primary text was not read; the record's quote comes through secondary reproductions.
